blocks.text: Spoken Word
Solo Whisper, No Music | Brief, intimate, impatient

There's a moment before you step out…
Five hundred coats still warm from the cold.
And somehow — they go quiet.
A glass hits the floor. An accordion inhales. GO.
Verse 1
Solo Voice, Barely Sung | Brisk crooked 3/4 begins in his footsteps

I'm drunk, the floor is drunk, we're both
just trying not to fall.
I can smell you from the door —
sweat and smoke and alcohol.
Refrain 1
Accordion joins from a doorway, tentative but moving

I feel the engine flood and choke,
I feel the pistons buck and stroke.
Verse 2
Keep Moving | Upright bass walks in, tambourine rattles from a pocket

My hands still shake — they always will —
this ain't a joke, this is the spill.
No one waits for you backstage,
just spit and whatever fills the cage.
Refrain 2
The Alley Gathers | Clarinet from a fire escape, brushed snare on a crate

Every eye a lantern lit,
every second — all of it.
Bridge
Faster, More Precarious | Instruments gathering, SOLO VOICE ONLY

This only happens once tonight,
this congregation, cracked and bright.
We're all just animals in clothes,
pretending someone here still knows.
Instrumental Acceleration
NO PAUSE | More players pile in without slowing the waltz: banjo, toy piano, tenor sax, battered percussion. Messier, faster, barely holding together.
Verse 3
Urgent, Breathless | Brass beginning to arrive

No algorithm knows this weight,
the hush before we levitate.
Standing small where God got lost —
come in, come in, forget the cost.
Final Refrain
Full Junkyard Orchestra | ONE SOLO VOICE fighting above it, no backing vocals

We choose the rust, we choose the flaw,
we choose to stand where feeling's raw.
We built this church from what was thrown away —
so welcome in.
Welcome in.
You're going to want to stay.
Outro
Spoken, Panting, Grinning | Orchestra still rattling behind him

The doors are open.
The band is loud.
The chairs don't match
and neither do we.
This is the Cathedral of Junk —

and every beautiful, broken one of you
belongs here tonight.
One enormous full-band hit. Cymbal crash. DEAD SILENCE.

notebook.style: Vaudeville waltz refracted as punk cabaret: fast crooked 3/4, one raspy high-tenor lead slipping into cracked theatrical falsetto, whispered footsteps opening into dry close-lofi talk-singing; accordion, bass, battered snare and banjo arrive singly, then clarinet, toy piano, sax and accelerating junkyard percussion, blues-jawk-folk-rock grit, brass arriving late, breathless shouting and abrupt silence
